name: foolish
//gen: tools/structgen reads the C headers through libclang and writes the modules sdk/, src/, server/ and e2e/ import (sdk/ts/gen, sdk/swift/gen). It is a BUILD STEP, not something a human remembers to run, so every script that compiles or loads those modules has a pre-hook: npm runs pre<name> before <name> automatically, including when the caller is a CI lane rather than a person. Generation is ~0.7s warm and any libclang writes the same bytes, so running it again costs a second and can never be wrong - a staleness cache here would be the one thing that could be.
//wasm: The same arrangement, one step along, for the three shipped wasm modules (scripts/wasm_build.sh). They used to be committed .gz files rebuilt by hand; they are build outputs now, so a lane that loads one builds it. TWO GROUPS, and the reason moved. All four modules have real per-object make rules now, so EVERY group is ~0s warm - measured per target on Linux/clang 18, warm: wasm-bots 0.21s, wasm-oracle 0.17s, wasm-oracle-mt 0.19s. The Oracle pair used to be the odd one out (phony targets whose recipes looped over all 34 sources in the shell, recompiling every run, ~10s), which is what the split was originally for. What the split is for NOW is the COLD build: from an empty c/build the Oracle pair is still ~13s of compiling, and a lane that cannot open an Oracle module has no use for it - a first-run tax is how a build step gets deleted. So the groups stay. scripts/wasm_build.sh's header has the measurements and the byte-identity check behind them. NOT hooked onto typecheck: tsc never opens a .gz, it is reached through `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` at runtime.

scripts.predev: npm run gen && npm run wasm
scripts.prebuild: npm run gen && npm run wasm
scripts.pretest:e2e: npm run gen && npm run wasm
scripts.pretest:validate: npm run gen && npm run wasm
scripts.//test:validate: No --test-concurrency: the validation files are pure functions with no Postgres and no shared state, so the 1 was inherited from the days when the whole suite shared one database. Measured, 104 tests either way: 8.77s at concurrency 1, 2.80s at node's default. This is the lane validate.yml runs on every push and every PR.
scripts.pretest:mem: npm run gen && npm run wasm:bots
scripts.//test:mem: --test-concurrency=1 stays here, unlike test:validate. These files measure wasm memory high-water marks, and a measurement taken while seven other node processes are competing for the same machine is a different measurement.
scripts.pretest:swift-parity: npm run gen && npm run wasm:bots
scripts.precoverage:e2e: npm run gen && npm run wasm
scripts.coverage:check: npm run coverage:check:server && npm run coverage:check:client
scripts.coverage: npm run coverage:e2e && npm run coverage:check
scripts.prebench:bot-e2e: npm run gen && npm run wasm:bots
scripts.premetrics: npm run gen && npm run wasm
